quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What do white lines on a roadway do?

options.text: Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Separate traffic moving in opposite directions.
Indicate a no passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Why is following closely behind a large truck a bad idea?

options.text: A good idea because you can draft off of the truck.
A good idea because other vehicles will get out of the way of a large truck.
A good idea because other motorists will be able to see you.
A bad idea because you might be in the truck's "no zone," an area where the truck driver cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: A bad idea because you might be in the truck's "no zone," an area where the truck driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots behind them. If you ride in this area, the truck driver cannot see you. The truck will also block your view of the road ahead.

questions.question: Before you start riding, the fuel valve should be:

options.text: Open.
Closed.
Covered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: The fuel valve must be open before you ride. If it is closed, the engine may start using fuel in the lines but will stall once that fuel runs out.

questions.question: _________ of motorcycle and car collisions are caused by drivers failing to yield to motorcyclists.

options.text: One-quarter
More than half
One-half

questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car collisions happen because drivers do not yield to motorcyclists. Never assume that drivers will yield the right-of-way, even if they are required to by law.

questions.question: Which check do you NOT need to make before riding?

options.text: Ensure that your tires have proper air pressure.
Ensure that the oil levels are safe.
Look under the motorcycle for leaks.
Ensure that the paint is shiny.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ensure that the paint is shiny.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure, tread, and wear. Check oil and fluid levels. Look for oil or gas leaks under the motorcycle. The paint does not need to be shiny.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal will soon turn red. Slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch?

options.text: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
You start to lose control in a curve.
The motorcycle starts to wobble.

questions.correctAnswerText: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, use the engine cut-off switch and pull the clutch at the same time. This removes power from the rear wheel so you can safely stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Which surface is potentially slippery?

options.text: A gravel road
A paved driveway
Dry pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: A gravel road
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and metal plates or utility covers.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to be seen.
Help you avoid surface hazards.
Invite other road users into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other road users into your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position should help you be seen, avoid hazards, wind blasts, and blind spots. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Your front wheel locks while you are braking. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop.
Keep squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake, then apply it again right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake, then apply it again right away.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure immediately. Then apply the brake again with steady, gradual pressure.

questions.question: When rain starts, where is the best place to ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
In the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull over to the side until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the oily strip in the center of the lane is slippery. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on both day and night to help others see you. Use your high beam whenever it is legal and safe. Also use your running lights if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to reduce the chances of a collision?

options.text: Stare straight ahead in front of the motorcycle.
Refuse to move to avoid a hazard.
Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds and scan your path of travel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds and scan your path of travel.
questions.explanation: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds on the road to reduce collision risk. This gives you time to react to a hazard before you reach it.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving on bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get across faster.
Ride in a zigzagging motion.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle starts to weave on bridge gratings, simply keep a steady speed and go straight across. Do not zigzag, as this is dangerous.

questions.question: When taking a curve with a group of riders, what formation should you use?

options.text: Single-file formation.
Pairs.
Staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups usually ride in a staggered formation. However, move into single-file when taking a curve, making a turn, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the operator.
Sidesaddle.
Behind the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit behind the operator and hold firmly to the operator's waist, hips, or midsection. They may hold onto handgrips if available. Never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: What can happen when you lock your brakes?

options.text: It helps in most situations.
It improves steering.
It can cause control problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause control problems.
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes can cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and then apply it again. If your rear brake locks on a good surface, keep it locked until you completely stop.

questions.question: Your front wheel locks while you are stopping. What should you do?

options.text: Keep applying the front brake.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks during a quick stop, release the front brake immediately and then apply it firmly again. Use both front and rear brakes for quick stops.

questions.question: What should riders do when using a roundabout?

options.text: Yield to entering traffic.
Move in a clockwise direction.
Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Increase speed before entering the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with traffic flowing counterclockwise around a center island. Enter from the right and yield to traffic already inside. Follow the circle to the right until you reach your exit.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay within the posted speed limit.
Go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to finish passing.
Pass more than one vehicle at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete all passes within the legal speed limit. Only pass when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that traffic ahead will merge.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn
No U-turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a staggered formation
In pairs
One at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcyclists in a group must pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for both the driver and passenger
Are not required

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have passenger footrests. Good footing keeps your passenger from falling and pulling you off too.
